title: Uygulamanın görsel kimliğini seç
question: Atanan yön Contour Atlas. Bu kimliği seç, alternatiflerden birini al veya yeni bir el iste.

options.label: Contour Atlas
options.lineage: Survey topography and national park maps
options.thesis: Household budgets become a clear landscape of named, readable money zones.
options.viewport: A deep green navigation rail frames a warm canvas; monthly income and remaining-to-budget lead, with envelope rows grouped into quiet terrain bands. Fine contour lines trace the selected envelope; all amounts and controls stay plain and high contrast.
options.risk: Contour lines can become decoration; they must stay sparse and never cross amounts or controls.

raised.raise: The screen now commits to a complete palette across shell, states, selection, and data, with one accent owning live focus.
The warm canvas and deep shell create one continuous environment instead of isolated floating cards.
Every annotation and category label stays explicitly attached to its amount and group.
The contour pattern is restrained to one meaningful selection state, leaving the rest of the surface quiet.
Budget states use clear labels and patterns alongside color, so no amount depends on hue alone.

options.label: Field Guide
options.thesis: A living household plan, organized like a beautifully precise field guide.
options.viewport: A compact navigation rail leads to a broad monthly overview; envelope groups read as labeled specimens with amounts, progress, and small botanical marks.
options.risk: Botanical illustration is familiar and can drift into lifestyle branding.

options.label: Garden Map
options.lineage: Public garden and zoo guide maps
options.thesis: Envelope groups form distinct, friendly regions in a household money map.
options.viewport: A familiar sidebar and month selector frame grouped envelope lists; selected groups receive a bold region color and amounts remain in clear rows.
options.case: Strong audience fit for family budgets; loses narrowly on dense financial data clarity.
options.risk: Large color regions may compete with transaction and balance reading.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: A precise visible grid gives every balance and envelope a deliberate place.
options.viewport: Standard app navigation and overview areas sit on a visible modular grid; a large monthly balance leads above tightly aligned account and envelope rows.
options.case: Excellent scanability, but its typographic formalism has less connection to household routines.
options.risk: Large constructed numerals can overpower ordinary transaction work.

options.label: Streaming Catalog Wall
options.case: Weakens both household identification and the clarity of dense budget data.
options.kept: A strong focus state that lets the active budget area stand out.
options.risk: Artwork tiles are a poor carrier for real transactions.

options.label: Centre Rail Reference Setting
options.case: Its two-column editorial form is less familiar and slower for routine budgeting.
options.kept: Labels and annotations remain visibly attached to the number they explain.
options.risk: Editorial columns can fragment a working budget screen.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.case: Encoded labels obscure household categories and everyday budget meaning.
options.kept: A distinctive, consistent signal can carry active selection across screens.
options.risk: Minimal coding can hide useful labels.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.lineage: Darkroom exposure records and zone scales
options.case: Its layered sheets add visual complexity to a routine household task.
options.kept: Money states carry explicit labels and non-color cues.
options.risk: Layered regions may imply confusing relationships between budgets.

canonCard.label: Category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished, conventional personal finance interface with quiet neutral surfaces.
canonCard.viewport: Standard sidebar navigation, month controls, a balance summary, and a readable envelope table.
canonCard.risk: Clear and familiar, with little identity of its own.
